items.title: US magnet recycler REEcycle clears an SEC hurdle for its planned Nasdaq listing via a SPAC
items.summary: The SEC has declared effective the registration statement for REEcycle's merger with Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp., a deal that values the Oklahoma rare-earth magnet recycler at about US$350 million plus a US$50 million earnout. Shareholders vote on 10 December, and REEcycle's first commercial plant is planned at roughly 160 tonnes a year of processing capacity.
items.why: A public listing for a magnet-to-oxide recycler gives Indian investors and recyclers a live valuation benchmark for rare-earth recovery from end-of-life magnets.
items.source: Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp. via GlobeNewswire

items.title: South Korea plans regulatory exemptions to recycle more cathode and anode scrap from battery plants
items.summary: At a 12 November meeting in Daejeon, South Korea's environment ministry said it will designate circular-economy zones with regulatory exemptions by the end of 2026 and back recycling trials through its regulatory sandbox in the first quarter of 2027. Companies asked for wider circular-resource eligibility so that production scrap now classed as waste faces lighter storage and transport rules.
items.why: With black mass exports now banned, Indian recyclers and cell makers will be watching how Korea frees up gigafactory scrap from waste rules, a model India's own battery-waste regime may need.

items.title: Korean firms commit 650 billion won to rare-earth magnet plants ahead of US defence sourcing curbs
items.summary: LS Cable & System will spend 350 billion won ($263 million) on a magnet plant in Gumi with more than 1,000 tonnes a year of capacity from 2028, while KMMI plans 300 billion won through 2030 for a 6,000-tonne plant in Pohang. The push comes before US rules from 1 January 2027 restrict China-sourced magnets across the whole defence supply chain.
items.why: Non-Chinese magnet capacity is growing fast in Asia, which raises demand for traceable rare-earth feed, including recycled material that Indian magnet and e-waste recyclers could supply.

items.title: Veolia opens a French hydrometallurgical plant able to process nearly 7,000 tonnes of black mass a year
items.summary: Veolia said on 12 November it has started a battery-metals recycling facility in France's Grand Est region that can treat nearly 7,000 tonnes of black mass a year, roughly 20,000 tonnes of batteries, recovering over 90% of the cobalt, nickel and copper. Feedstock will come from France, the UK and Switzerland, and Veolia expects close to 700,000 tonnes of batteries to reach recycling in Europe within five years.
items.why: More refining capacity in Europe adds buyers for black mass just as India has banned its export, so Indian recyclers will be competing with hubs like this for feedstock and offtake partners rather than selling to them.

items.title: China's magnet-scrap prices hold at highs as dysprosium oxide climbs past 1.5 million yuan a tonne
items.summary: SMM's weekly review puts Pr-Nd recovered from NdFeB scrap at 715–720 yuan/kg, recycled dysprosium at 1,230–1,250 yuan/kg and recycled terbium at 5,600–5,800 yuan/kg after successive gains. Dysprosium oxide rose sharply to 1.51–1.52 million yuan/mt and Pr-Nd oxide to 715,000–718,000 yuan/mt as of 12 November.
items.why: Firm heavy rare earth prices improve the economics of recovering magnets from Indian e-waste and motors, a segment the critical-mineral recycling scheme is meant to build up.

items.title: COSMO AM&T and Carbon Resources plan a ₹40 billion LFP cathode plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh's cabinet on 10 November approved a ₹40 billion plan by South Korea's COSMO AM&T and India's Carbon Resources for a battery materials plant at Naidupeta in Tirupati district. The first phase, targeted for mid-2028, would make 30,000 tonnes a year each of iron phosphate precursor and LFP cathode material, rising to 180,000 tonnes each (360,000 tonnes combined) by 2031.
items.why: A large domestic LFP cathode maker would be a natural local buyer for lithium recovered by Indian recyclers, which matters more now that black mass can no longer be exported.

items.title: India bans exports of lithium-ion battery black mass with immediate effect
items.summary: A DGFT notification moves battery waste and scrap under ITC (HS) code 85491400 from 'Free' to 'Prohibited' until further orders, covering unsorted scrap free of lead, cadmium and mercury, which the notice identifies as lithium-ion black mass. The change is limited to that category and is not a blanket ban on all battery material.
items.why: Indian shredders that sold black mass abroad must now find domestic refiners, which should shift payables and favour recyclers with their own hydrometallurgy capacity.

items.title: LS MnM opens an Ulsan battery materials plant that can take black mass as well as MHP
items.summary: The South Korean smelter completed the plant at its Onsan site on 10 November, with nickel sulfate capacity equal to 24,000 tonnes of contained nickel a year. It will also make cobalt sulfate, manganese sulfate and lithium hydroxide for precursor makers.
items.why: More Korean refining capacity that accepts black mass adds to the buyers Asian recyclers can sell to, a market Indian exporters are now shut out of.

items.title: Germany's Tozero makes first delivery of recycled lithium carbonate under a long-term contract
items.summary: Tozero shipped lithium carbonate from its Gendorf demonstration plant, sized for about 500 tonnes of battery waste a year, to ceramic-colour maker Botz under a binding supply deal. The startup aims to recover over 80% of the lithium in used batteries and sells mainly to construction, ceramics and lubricant buyers for now.
items.why: It shows small black-mass refiners can earn early revenue from non-battery lithium buyers while working towards battery grade, a path open to Indian start-ups too.

items.title: Ecoprogetti's automated solar panel recycling line is running in northern Italy
items.summary: Ecoprogetti has supplied a fully automated module recycling line to a site in Sale, Italy, run by Raee.man, a subsidiary of Haiki+. The line can handle up to 120 panels an hour and has reported 94% uptime since it began operating in early 2025.
items.why: Indian module makers and recyclers preparing for MNRE's coming solar recycling guidelines can use this as a benchmark for what a commercial automated line delivers.

items.title: China's black mass payables fell through October, with LCO dropping hardest
items.summary: SMM says the lithium payable for LCO black mass slid from above 70% to about 63% in October, while ternary black mass cobalt payables fell from 73.46% to 68.9% and lithium payables to 70.02%. The cuts followed a month in which lithium carbonate fell more than 20% and cobalt sulfate over 25%.
items.why: Lower Chinese payables set the benchmark Indian black mass sellers are quoted against, squeezing margins for recyclers that sell rather than refine.

items.title: Rivian widens Redwood Materials deal to cover scrap, end-of-life packs and second-life storage
items.summary: Redwood Materials will recycle Rivian's production scrap and retired EV batteries collected through Rivian's service centres, deciding pack by pack whether to reuse or recycle. An earlier April 2026 deal is already deploying 10 MWh of storage built from repurposed Rivian packs at its Normal, Illinois plant, and Redwood says it recovers over 95% of lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.
items.why: It shows the full-lifecycle OEM–recycler contract that Indian EV makers may need to meet battery EPR targets, combining reuse and recycling under one partner.

items.title: China extends its pause on wider rare earth export controls by two months, to 10 January
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce said on 9 November that the one-year suspension of its October 2025 expansion of rare earth export controls, which also covered lithium battery technology, will run two more months until 10 January. The move is part of a wider pause in trade countermeasures as Beijing negotiates a lasting deal with Washington ahead of an expected Xi–Trump meeting at APEC in Shenzhen.
items.why: A short two-month window keeps rare earth and magnet supply uncertain, which supports the case for Indian magnet and battery recyclers building domestic sources of these materials.

items.title: US EPA says its draft universal-waste rule for lithium-ion batteries and solar panels may be out for comment in spring
items.summary: EPA officials told state waste regulators that the draft rule, first promised in 2023, is still being written and could be proposed for public comment in the spring, with the federal agenda pencilling in a final rule for August 2027. State officials estimate only about 5% of US lithium batteries are recycled, and a House-passed bill would force EPA to finish a lithium-ion rule within 18 months.
items.why: Clearer US rules on collecting and storing spent lithium-ion batteries and end-of-life panels would change how much feedstock stays with US recyclers, which shapes export competition and partnership openings for Indian battery and solar recyclers.

items.title: MNRE is drafting solar module recycling guidelines that will push makers to build more recyclable panels
items.summary: MNRE Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi said at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit that the ministry wants the guidelines out quickly; solar and wind waste currently falls under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, which require waste modules to be preserved until 2035. Suzlon and the Aditya Birla Group signed an MoU to recycle blade epoxy, and MNRE plans an SOP to extend this to other wind turbine makers.
items.why: Separate product-specific rules for solar and wind waste would reshape EPR obligations for module makers and open a dedicated feedstock stream for Indian recyclers ahead of the 2033–35 wave of retiring panels.

items.title: China LFP black mass prices edge down again while ternary payables hold steady
items.summary: SMM said lithium carbonate consolidated around 92,000 yuan per tonne as of 5 November, while LFP black mass prices were adjusted down modestly and cobalt payables for ternary material slipped slightly. LCO black mass payables remain near their lowest levels of the past year, with trading described as sluggish and buyers waiting.
items.why: Chinese black mass payables set the benchmark against which Indian shredders price their output and judge whether exporting or refining locally pays.

items.title: Wagga residents press NSW planning commission to reject a 3,000-tonne lithium-ion battery recycling hub
items.summary: The NSW Independent Planning Commission held public meetings on 3 and 4 November on Calibre Metals' proposed battery recycling hub in East Wagga, which the developer says could process at most 3,000 tonnes a year. The planning department received more than 50 community submissions opposing it, with flood risk a recurring concern, and written submissions stay open until 11 November.
items.why: Local opposition over fire and flood risk is a hurdle Indian battery recyclers also face when siting plants, and shows why site choice and safety cases matter for approvals.

items.title: Comstock Metals says its Nevada solar panel recycling line now runs continuously
items.summary: Comstock Metals reports that its solar panel recycling system at Silver Springs, Nevada has moved to continuous operation across four shift teams and will now ramp up production. It also says extra storage for incoming panels is in place at its Hanford, California and Cambridge, Ohio sites.
items.why: Commercial-scale panel recycling running round the clock in the US is a reference point for India, which has yet to build dedicated capacity for its own coming wave of solar waste.

items.title: Cabinet clears ₹2,814 crore capex subsidy for two lithium and two nickel processing plants
items.summary: The five-year scheme (FY27 to FY31) offers a 30% capital subsidy to four units, each lithium plant needing at least 30,000 tonnes of capacity and each nickel plant at least 50,000 tonnes, with cobalt recovered as a by-product of nickel. Support is capped at ₹500 crore per lithium beneficiary and ₹900 crore per nickel beneficiary, picked through technical qualification followed by bidding on the lowest capital support sought.
items.why: It funds the step of turning ores and intermediates into high-purity battery compounds, which India largely lacks today; whether recycled intermediates such as black mass qualify will decide how much it helps Indian battery recyclers.

items.title: Wayanad gathers 80 tonnes of e-waste in a 50-day drive to become India's first e-waste-free district
items.summary: The Kerala campaign, launched on 10 September, covered all 23 village panchayats and three municipalities, with government offices handing in 31 tonnes and Noolpuzha becoming the first e-waste-free panchayat on 27 October after collecting 5,423 kg. A buffer period with a complaints call centre runs to 10 November, before a formal declaration at Kalpetta on 20 November.
items.why: If other districts copy this government-led model, more household and office e-waste could move into formal collection, the feedstock India's EPR-registered recyclers compete for.

items.title: Lead industry body wants India's battery dealers made accountable for collecting spent batteries
items.summary: India Lead Zinc Development Association executive director L Pugazhenthy says the Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 leave dealers' duties unclear, and wants dealers registered, collections reported and recyclers audited regularly rather than approved once. About 30% of India's recycled lead still comes from the informal sector and about 65% from authorised recyclers, even though authorised capacity of about 3.5 million tonnes is well above secondary lead output of about 1.6 million tonnes.
items.why: Tighter dealer and audit rules would steer more spent lead-acid batteries to authorised recyclers and change how producers meet their battery EPR targets.

items.title: Japan proposes that owners scrapping 50 tonnes or more of solar panels file disposal plans in advance
items.summary: Japan's environment ministry and METI favour a 50-tonne threshold that would cover about 7,398 facilities and roughly 38% of expected panel waste from 2027 to 2050, under a solar recycling law due to take effect around December 2027. Panel waste is now projected to peak at up to about 500,000 tonnes a year in the 2040s, well above earlier estimates.
items.why: Japan's volume-based trigger is a working template for India as it decides how to make large solar plant owners handle their own coming wave of end-of-life modules.

items.title: Sumitomo moves past an MoU to study black mass processing at Livium's Melbourne site
items.summary: Sumitomo Corporation and Livium's Envirostream unit are now evaluating technology, equipment, economics and approvals for expanding black mass output at Derrimut, Victoria, with possible refining in Japan. Sumitomo has started onboarding for a potential black mass purchase, but no binding deal, volumes or pricing are agreed, and Envirostream's existing SungEel HiTech offtake runs to June 2027.
items.why: Japanese trading houses lining up black mass from smaller markets is the same feedstock competition Indian recyclers face as they try to keep black mass at home.

items.title: Fraunhofer and TU Freiberg test two new routes to recover neodymium from hard-drive magnets
items.summary: The four-year, Horizon Europe-funded NEO-CYCLE project is trialling solid-state chlorination with ammonium chloride and an electrochemical process to separate neodymium, iron and boron from scrapped magnets, with a pilot plant already being planned. Fraunhofer notes about 90% of Europe's neodymium comes from China and most magnets collected in Europe are shipped there for reprocessing.
items.why: Hard drives are a large part of India's e-waste stream, so low-chemical magnet recovery routes are directly relevant to recyclers eyeing rare earths under the critical-mineral recycling scheme.

items.title: Malaysian battery recycler Econili adds Vynn Capital, taking total funding to RM8 million
items.summary: Econili, one of five licensed battery-recycling operators in Malaysia, has 24,000 tonnes a year of battery treatment and 12,000 tonnes of critical-mineral recovery capacity in Ipoh, recovering lithium, nickel and cobalt. The undisclosed Vynn Capital cheque brings total funding to about RM8 million (US$1.96 million), to be used to buy more feedstock and raise throughput.
items.why: Southeast Asian recyclers raising money to buy more battery scrap adds to regional competition for the feedstock Indian recyclers also import.

items.title: GST reverse charge now applies to e-waste scrap bought from unregistered sellers
items.summary: From 1 November 2026, a registered business that buys electrical and electronic waste and scrap (tariff item 8549) from an unregistered supplier must pay the GST itself under reverse charge, under Notification No. 04/2026 dated 27 October 2026. The same change covers plastic scrap, tyre scrap and used cooking oil, and was made on the GST Council's recommendation.
items.why: Recyclers and dismantlers that source e-waste from informal kabadiwalas now carry the GST liability and paperwork on those purchases, which changes sourcing costs and pushes the chain toward registered suppliers.

items.title: China's GEM recycled 50,105 tonnes of EV batteries in January–September, up over 36%
items.summary: GEM, one of China's largest battery recyclers, says it recycled and dismantled 50,105 tonnes of power batteries in the first three quarters of 2026. That is more than 36% higher than a year earlier, according to its third-quarter report.
items.why: Fast-growing Chinese recyclers set the scale and cost benchmark that Indian battery recyclers and black mass buyers will have to compete against.

items.title: Odisha plans a rare-earth corridor around Gopalpur, from beach-sand mining to magnet making
items.summary: Odisha is drawing up an integrated rare-earth cluster on the Ganjam-Puri coast covering extraction, separation, metals and permanent magnets, building on its roughly 3.16 million tonnes of monazite (of 13.15 million tonnes nationally). The state has approved five projects with proposed investment of about ₹26,450 crore and around 18,450 jobs, while the Mining Corporation of Odisha is acquiring new beach-sand blocks.
items.why: Rare earth chloride from IREL's Odisha plant is now processed elsewhere, so a local magnet supply chain would create domestic offtake, and future scrap streams, for India's planned magnet recyclers.

items.title: Australia faces 1.1 million tonnes of dead solar panels by 2035 and needs national rules now, RAND–RMIT brief warns
items.summary: A policy brief by RAND and RMIT University, sponsored by Australia's industry department, projects cumulative end-of-life solar waste of 1.1 million tonnes by 2035, possibly tripling by 2050, and urges a national PV circularity framework by mid-2027 and federal funding for recycling plants by 2028. It values recoverable silver at more than A$6 billion (about US$4.2 billion) a year by 2035 and finds a 2,500-tonne-a-year recycling plant could pay back in 7.2 to 8 years in five states.
items.why: India's solar fleet is growing far faster than Australia's, so the brief's plant economics and reuse-first approach are a useful benchmark for Indian recyclers planning panel capacity.

items.title: Gravita's September-quarter revenue rises 38% to ₹1,427 crore as its new copper business adds volume
items.summary: Gravita India reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹1,427 crore and net profit of ₹102 crore (up 6%), with the integrated copper business contributing ₹420 crore. Lead recycling volume fell 11.3% to 39,203 tonnes on scrap shortages linked to West Asia and Red Sea shipping delays, and the company plans ₹1,680 crore of capex through FY29, including ₹865 crore for new verticals such as copper and lithium-ion battery recycling.
items.why: A listed Indian recycler is committing capital to lithium-ion and copper recycling, while its lead numbers show how exposed scrap-fed recyclers are to import supply disruptions.

items.title: MIDHANI signs MoU with BARC and the Heavy Water Board to recover nickel and cobalt from plant reverts
items.summary: Defence PSU Mishra Dhatu Nigam (MIDHANI) signed a three-way MoU with the Heavy Water Board and BARC to develop efficient recovery processes for nickel and cobalt from its plant reverts. The pact is a cooperation framework; no capacity, investment or timeline was disclosed.
items.why: It brings state research labs into recovering nickel and cobalt from secondary material, the same metals India's battery recyclers and the critical-minerals push are targeting.

items.title: European clean-tech groups ask the EU to weigh export fees on black mass as most of it leaves the bloc
items.summary: Transport & Environment, Recharge, Clean Tech for Europe and EIES urged the EU to assess export fees or tariffs on black mass and untreated battery waste in its Circular Economy Act, along with a single customs code and end-of-waste criteria for the material. T&E estimates at least 60% of Europe's black mass is exported for refining and says over half of the region's battery recycling capacity is at risk.
items.why: Curbs on European black mass exports would shrink the traded supply that refiners elsewhere, including India's new hydrometallurgy plants, compete for.

items.title: China black mass payables slip again as lithium carbonate falls back to about 90,000 yuan a tonne
items.summary: Lithium carbonate futures jumped early in the week but were back near 90,000 yuan a tonne by 29 October, SMM reports, and LFP black mass prices held at first before easing with them. Ternary and LCO payable indicators edged down alongside nickel, cobalt and lithium and now sit near their lowest in about a year, with cobalt payables settling below nickel and lithium.
items.why: Chinese payables are the benchmark for black mass sold out of India, so weaker payables cut what Indian shredders can earn on their output.

items.title: China's recycled Pr-Nd from magnet scrap slips to 715–720 yuan/kg as oxide prices weaken
items.summary: SMM says recycled Pr-Nd from NdFeB scrap fell through the week to 715–720 yuan/kg as recyclers cut their quotes in step with lower Pr-Nd oxide, while dysprosium (1,230–1,250 yuan/kg) and terbium (5,600–5,800 yuan/kg) held steady. Suppliers resisted selling at lower prices, trading stayed thin, and SMM expects scrap prices to remain weak in the short term.
items.why: Scrap Pr-Nd prices shape the economics of the magnet-recycling capacity Indian firms are planning alongside the rare earth magnet scheme.

items.title: India's official e-waste numbers and TERI's estimate are still far apart, and EPR checks rely largely on paperwork
items.summary: CPCB figures given to the Lok Sabha show India generated about 1.397 million tonnes of e-waste in 2024-25 and recycled about 1.159 million tonnes, while a TERI report prepared with NITI Aayog support estimates 6.19 million tonnes for 2024, with only 22% reaching authorised recyclers. TERI, which counts 381 registered recyclers and 128 refurbishers, says EPR audits rely mostly on paper checklists and that the GSTN and EPR portals are not linked, weakening invoice tracing.
items.why: If regulators move to material-balance tests or third-party audits of recyclers, as industry voices in the piece propose, the supply and price of EPR certificates that producers buy could shift.

items.title: Australia's A$24.7 million solar panel recycling pilot has been on hold for over five months
items.summary: The federal pilot, meant to set up as many as 100 collection sites for old panels, was suspended on 15 May after a single complaint under procurement rules, and the environment department could not say when it will restart. Australia had about 3 million panels (60,000 tonnes) reach end of life in 2025, a figure that could hit 50 million panels (1 million tonnes) by 2035, with as little as 17% recycled.
items.why: India's own solar fleet will throw up similar volumes, and Australia shows how slowly collection systems get built without a clear, enforced rulebook.

items.title: African governments move towards EPR for solar panels and batteries as installations surge
items.summary: Nigeria has validated a policy that would make producers, distributors and importers of off-grid solar gear responsible for it at end of life, pending cabinet approval, and ECOWAS energy ministers adopted a regional framework on handling and recycling storage batteries. Ember expects Africa to install a record 17 GW of solar in 2026, roughly 100,000 panels a day.
items.why: New EPR regimes in fast-growing solar markets could open export and partnership routes for Indian panel and battery recyclers.

items.title: Korean black mass payables drop to their lowest since January as LME Week mood sours
items.summary: Fastmarkets' NCM black mass payables (cif South Korea) fell to 88-94% for nickel and cobalt on 21 October, from 92-96% a week earlier, the weakest it has recorded since 21 January 2026. Traders at LME Week pointed to Korean cellmakers moving to LFP, with one recycler saying Korean pCAM and CAM plants are running at only about 20% capacity.
items.why: Lower Asian payables cut what Indian recyclers can earn by exporting NCM black mass and strengthen the case for refining it at home.

items.title: HyProMag USA plans three more US magnet recycling plants to quadruple output to about 4,200 tonnes a year
items.summary: A pre-feasibility study puts new plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second Texas site at about $623–656 million, lifting salable NdFeB magnet output to roughly 4,192 tonnes a year by 2034 from about 1,048 tonnes at its first plant in Northlake, Texas. The study, which modelled a recycled-scrap-only case among others, estimates a post-tax NPV of $1.85–2.06 billion; Northlake's first phase is due in mid-2028 and no offtake deals are signed yet.
items.why: Magnet scrap is becoming a contested feedstock outside China, which matters for Indian recyclers that collect NdFeB scrap from motors and electronics and for India's planned magnet plants.

items.title: Taiwan's ITRI plans a 500-tonne-a-year rare earth plant to meet half the island's needs by 2030
items.summary: ITRI president Chang Pei-zen says a demonstration plant making 500 tonnes of rare earths a year is targeted for completion by end-2028, a hundredfold scale-up from the institute's experimental line of about 5,000 kg a year. The goal is to cover half of Taiwan's demand by end-2030 and cut exposure to Chinese export restrictions, with state funding and possible price guarantees still under discussion.
items.why: It is another electronics-heavy economy building rare earth separation outside China, the same supply gap India's magnet and critical-mineral recycling schemes are trying to close.
